items.definition: An animal is a living thing that moves and eats, like a dog, a bird, or a fish.
items.example: A horse is a big animal.
items.picture_idea: A dog, a cat, and a bird sitting together
items.definition_previous: A living thing that can move and eat, like a dog, bird, or fish.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a living organism characterized by voluntary movement

items.definition: An apple is a round fruit that you can eat. Its skin can be red, green, or yellow.
items.example: I ate a red apple for lunch.
items.picture_idea: A shiny red apple with a leaf
items.definition_previous: A round fruit that is red, green, or yellow.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: fruit with red or yellow or green skin and sweet to tart crisp whitish flesh

items.definition: A baby is a very young child. Babies drink milk, sleep a lot, and cannot walk or talk yet.
items.example: The baby is sleeping in her bed.
items.picture_idea: A smiling baby in a crib
items.definition_previous: A very young child who cannot walk or talk yet.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a very young child (birth to 1 year) who has not yet begun to walk or talk

items.definition: A ball is a round thing used in games. You throw it, kick it, or hit it.
items.example: She kicked the ball across the grass.
items.picture_idea: A child kicking a ball on a field
items.definition_previous: A round thing that you throw, kick, or hit in games.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: round object that is hit or thrown or kicked in games

items.definition: Beautiful means very nice to look at or to hear. A beautiful flower or song can make you smile.
items.example: The garden looks beautiful in spring.
items.picture_idea: A garden full of colorful flowers
items.definition_previous: Very nice to look at or hear.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: delighting the senses or exciting intellectual or emotional admiration

items.definition: Use big to tell how large something is. A big box takes up a lot of room.
items.example: The elephant is very big.
items.picture_idea: A big elephant next to a small mouse
items.definition_previous: Large in size.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: above average in size or number or quantity or magnitude or extent

items.definition: You bring something when you carry it with you to a place. Bring your coat if it is cold.
items.example: Please bring your book to school.
items.picture_idea: A child carrying a book to a classroom
items.definition_previous: To carry something with you to a place.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take something or somebody with oneself somewhere

items.definition: A brother is a boy or man who has the same parents as you, or one of the same parents.
items.example: My brother plays soccer with me.
items.picture_idea: Two boys playing together
items.definition_previous: A boy or man who has the same parents as you.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a male with the same parents as someone else

items.definition_batch: A brother is a boy or man who has the same mother and father as you.

items.definition: Use but when the second part of what you say is different or surprising. I wanted to play, but it rained.
items.example: I like cake, but I do not like pie.
items.definition_previous: A word used to show something different or surprising.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You climb when you go up something, using your hands and feet. You can climb a tree or a ladder.
items.explanation: The b in climb is silent.
items.example: The cat likes to climb the tree.
items.picture_idea: A child climbing a ladder on a playground
items.definition_previous: To go up something using your hands and feet.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move with effort, by grasping

items.definition: Cold describes something with very little heat. Ice and snow are cold, and you may shiver.
items.example: The water in the lake is cold.
items.picture_idea: A child in a coat and hat in the snow
items.definition_previous: Having a low temperature; not warm.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: having a low or inadequate temperature or feeling a sensation of coldness or having been made cold by e.g. ice or refrigeration

items.definition: Use come when you move toward a person or place. Say "Come here!" to ask someone to move to you.
items.example: Please come to my house after school.
items.picture_idea: A girl waving to a friend to come closer
items.definition_previous: To move toward a person or place.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move toward, travel toward something or somebody or approach something or somebody

items.definition: When you dance, you move your body in time to music. You can dance alone or with other people.
items.explanation: Dance can also be a noun, as in 'a dance'.
items.example: We dance when our favorite song plays.
items.picture_idea: Children dancing in a circle to music
items.definition_previous: To move your body to music.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move in a pattern; usually to musical accompaniment; do or perform a dance

items.definition: When you draw, you make a picture with a pencil, pen, or crayon. You draw on paper.
items.example: I like to draw pictures of animals.
items.picture_idea: A child drawing with crayons on paper
items.definition_previous: To make a picture with a pencil, pen, or crayon.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: represent by making a drawing of, as with a pencil, chalk, etc. on a surface

items.definition: You eat when you chew food and swallow it. Say eat when you want food or it is mealtime.
items.example: We eat lunch at noon.
items.picture_idea: A child eating a sandwich at a table
items.definition_previous: To put food in your mouth and swallow it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: take in solid food

items.definition: An egg is an oval food with a hard shell. Hens lay eggs, and we cook them to eat.
items.explanation: Baby birds also grow inside eggs.
items.example: I had an egg for breakfast.
items.picture_idea: A white egg in an egg cup
items.definition_previous: An oval food with a hard shell, laid by a hen.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: oval reproductive body of a fowl (especially a hen) used as food

items.definition: Use every to talk about each one in a group, with none left out, like every day of the week.
items.example: Every child got a new pencil.
items.definition_previous: Each one of a group, with none left out.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Fast means going a long way in a short time. A fast runner gets to the end quickly.
items.explanation: Fast can also be an adverb, as in 'run fast'.
items.example: The rabbit is very fast.
items.picture_idea: A rabbit running quickly past a turtle
items.definition_previous: Able to move or happen quickly.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: acting or moving or capable of acting or moving quickly

items.definition: Use feel to tell how your body or mind is right now. You might feel tired, happy, or sick.
items.example: I feel happy when I see my friends.
items.picture_idea: A child touching a soft blanket with a smile
items.definition_previous: To have a feeling in your body or your mind.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be conscious of a physical, mental, or emotional state

items.definition: When you find something, you see it or get it after looking for it. You can find a lost toy.
items.example: I cannot find my red shoe.
items.picture_idea: A child looking under a bed and finding a shoe
items.definition_previous: To see or get something you were looking for.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: come upon after searching; find the location of something that was missed or lost

items.definition: A friend is someone you know well and like. You enjoy talking and playing together.
items.example: My friend shares her crayons with me.
items.picture_idea: Two children holding hands and smiling
items.definition_previous: A person you like and enjoy being with.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a person you know well and regard with affection and trust

items.definition: Use give when you hand someone something so they have it. Say "Give me that" when you want it.
items.example: I will give you a pencil.
items.picture_idea: One child handing a gift to another
items.definition_previous: To hand something to another person so they have it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: transfer possession of something concrete or abstract to somebody

items.definition: Use go to talk about moving from one place to another. Say "Let's go!" when you are ready to leave.
items.example: We go to school by bus.
items.picture_idea: Children walking toward a school bus
items.definition_previous: To move from one place to another.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: change location; move, travel, or proceed, also metaphorically

items.definition: You are happy when you feel good and full of joy. Say happy when you smile or laugh.
items.example: The puppy is happy to see me.
items.picture_idea: A smiling child jumping with joy
items.definition_previous: Feeling good and full of joy.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: enjoying or showing or marked by joy or pleasure

items.definition: Say he when you talk about one boy or man and you do not say his name.
items.example: He is my brother, and he likes to draw.
items.picture_idea: A boy with an arrow pointing to him
items.definition_previous: A word for a boy or man when you are not saying his name.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say hello when you meet someone, or when you answer the phone.
items.example: Hello, my name is Sam.
items.picture_idea: Two children waving at each other
items.definition_previous: A word you say when you meet someone.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Help means to make a job easier for someone. You say "Help me!" when you need a hand.
items.explanation: Help can also be a noun, and people call out 'Help!' when they need it.
items.example: I help my dad make dinner.
items.picture_idea: A child helping an adult carry a bag
items.definition_previous: To do something useful for another person.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: give help or assistance; be of service

items.definition: Here means the place where you are right now. You say here when you point to a spot close to you.
items.example: Put your bag here, please.
items.picture_idea: A child pointing to the ground next to them
items.definition_previous: In this place or to this place.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: in or at this place; where the speaker or writer is

items.definition: Hot means having a lot of heat. Soup, a stove, or the sun can feel hot.
items.example: Be careful, the soup is hot.
items.picture_idea: A steaming bowl of soup
items.definition_previous: Having a lot of heat; very warm.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: used of physical heat; having a high or higher than desirable temperature or giving off heat or feeling or causing a sensation of heat or burning

items.definition: A house is a building where people live. It has rooms, a roof, and a door.
items.example: Our house has a green door.
items.picture_idea: A small house with a door, windows, and a roof
items.definition_previous: A building where people live.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a dwelling that serves as living quarters for one or more families

items.definition: You use how to ask the way something is done, or to ask how someone is feeling.
items.example: How do you tie your shoes?
items.definition_previous: A word used to ask about the way something is done or how someone is.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say I when you talk about yourself. If you want a drink, you say, "I want a drink."
items.explanation: I is always written with a capital letter.
items.example: I like to read books.
items.picture_idea: A child pointing to their own chest
items.definition_previous: The word you use to talk about yourself.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say in when something is inside a thing, with its sides all around it, like a toy in a box or milk in a cup.
items.example: The toy is in the box.
items.picture_idea: A toy bear inside a box
items.definition_previous: Inside something or within a place.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition_batch: You say in when something has sides around it, like a toy in a box or milk in a cup.

edited.why: the batch wording said the thing inside has sides around it, which is backwards

items.definition: To jump is to push off the ground with your feet and go up into the air. Frogs jump a lot.
items.example: The children jump over the puddle.
items.picture_idea: A child jumping over a puddle
items.definition_previous: To push yourself up off the ground into the air.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move forward by leaps and bounds

items.definition: Kind means caring about others and being nice to them. A kind friend shares a snack with you.
items.explanation: Kind can also be a noun meaning a type, as in 'a kind of fruit'.
items.example: She is kind to everyone in her class.
items.picture_idea: A child helping a smaller child up after a fall
items.definition_previous: Caring and good to other people.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: having or showing a tender and considerate and helpful nature; used especially of persons and their behavior

items.definition: You say know when a fact is in your mind and you are sure of it. If not, say "I don't know."
items.explanation: The k in know is silent.
items.example: I know the answer to that question.
items.picture_idea: A child raising a hand with a bright idea
items.definition_previous: To have something in your mind as a fact; to be sure about it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be cognizant or aware of a fact or a specific piece of information; possess knowledge or information about

items.definition: You laugh when something is funny. It makes a happy "ha ha" sound.
items.explanation: The gh in laugh sounds like f.
items.example: We laugh at the funny clown.
items.picture_idea: Children laughing at a clown
items.definition_previous: To make happy sounds with your voice because something is funny.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: produce laughter

items.definition: You say you like something when you enjoy it or think it is good. Say "I like it!" to tell someone.
items.explanation: Like can also be a preposition meaning 'the same as', as in 'big like a bear'.
items.example: I like pizza.
items.picture_idea: A child smiling with a thumbs up next to a pizza
items.definition_previous: To enjoy something or think it is good.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: find enjoyable or agreeable

items.definition: To listen is to use your ears and pay attention to a sound or to someone talking.
items.explanation: The t in listen is silent.
items.example: Please listen to the teacher.
items.picture_idea: A child with a hand cupped behind an ear
items.definition_previous: To pay attention to a sound or to what someone says.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: listen and pay attention

items.definition: Long means measuring a lot from one end to the other. A rope or a road can be long.
items.example: The snake is very long.
items.picture_idea: A long snake stretched out beside a short pencil
items.definition_previous: Measuring a lot from one end to the other.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: primarily spatial sense; of relatively great or greater than average spatial extension or extension as specified

items.definition: You look when you point your eyes at something to see it. Say "Look!" to get someone to see it too.
items.example: Look at the pretty bird!
items.picture_idea: A child pointing at a bird in a tree
items.definition_previous: To use your eyes to see something.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: perceive with attention; direct one's gaze towards; look

items.definition: You say make when you use things to build or cook something new. You can make a cake or a snowman.
items.example: We make a snowman every winter.
items.picture_idea: Children building a snowman
items.definition_previous: To build, cook, or create something.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: create or manufacture a man-made product

items.definition: Many means a big number of things you can count. There are many stars in the sky.
items.explanation: Use many with things you can count, like books or birds.
items.example: There are many stars in the sky.
items.picture_idea: A night sky full of stars
items.definition_previous: A large number of things or people.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say more when you want extra of something. If you have one cookie and want another, say "more."
items.explanation: More can also be an adverb, as in 'Please play more'.
items.example: Can I have more juice, please?
items.picture_idea: A child holding out an empty cup for a refill
items.definition_previous: A bigger amount, or an extra amount of something.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Morning is the first part of the day, after the sun comes up and before lunch time.
items.example: I brush my teeth every morning.
items.picture_idea: A sun rising over a house while a child wakes up
items.definition_previous: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the time period between dawn and noon

items.definition: A mother is a woman who is a parent. A child may call her Mom.
items.example: My mother reads me a story at night.
items.picture_idea: A mother hugging her child
items.definition_previous: A woman who has a child.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a woman who has given birth to a child (also used as a term of address to your mother)

items.definition_batch: A mother is a woman who has a baby or a child. A baby grows inside its mother before birth.

edited.why: the birth sentence leaves out adoptive, foster and step mothers; broader than WordNet's meaning on purpose

items.definition: The mouth is the opening in your face where food goes in and sounds come out.
items.example: Open your mouth wide for the dentist.
items.picture_idea: A smiling face with the mouth highlighted
items.definition_previous: The part of your face you use to eat and talk.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the opening through which food is taken in and vocalizations emerge

items.definition: Money is the coins and paper bills you give to buy things. A shop takes money for its things.
items.explanation: Money is not usually used in the plural.
items.example: I saved my money to buy a toy.
items.picture_idea: A handful of coins and a dollar bill
items.definition_previous: Coins and paper bills that you use to buy things.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the most common medium of exchange; functions as legal tender
